Tiszavasvari Jewish Cemetery in Bud

Jewish Cemetery · Tiszavasvári, Hungary

Demolished. This is the second of two historic Jewish cemeteries within modern Tiszavasvári, serving the community of Büd. Jews settled in the area at the end of the 18th century, with the organized community established in 1840; the population grew from 104 in 1828 to 732 by 1930. Following the German occupation, the town's Jews were gathered in spring 1944 and deported via the Nyíregyháza Ghetto to Auschwitz, with 557 murdered in the Holocaust; only about 70 survivors returned, and the last Jews left during the 1956 Hungarian Uprising.
